ai.description: This gecko reaches 70 mm SVL. It is grey-brown with dark dorsal blotches and a smooth back. Distinctive features include extensive lateral skin flaps and fully webbed digits for gliding.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gekko lionotum* is best distinguished by its smooth, granular dorsal scales that lack the enlarged, prominent tubercles found on most other Indian *Gekko* species.
ai.habitat: *Gekko lionotum* inhabits tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Indian subcontinent, typically found on tree trunks in lowland areas below 500 meters.
ai.behavior: Gekko lionotum is primarily nocturnal and uses its specialized skin flaps to glide between trees, an effective strategy for escaping predators or traversing the canopy.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gekko lionotum* is oviparous, laying clutches of two hard-shelled, adhesive eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gekko lionotum* is found in Northeast India, specifically within the states of Mizoram and Tripura, inhabiting lowland forests at low to moderate elevations.
